subject: Request: AWS marketplace listing discount appeal & syndication credit — CloudBroker
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@cloudbroker.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0400
Subject: Listing discount request for CloudBroker - AWS marketplace syndication

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team at CloudBroker is very excited about Redwood. We have one gating item before we can move forward with the AWS listing: a competing vendor (EdgeServe) is offering a 35% listing fee concession + co-sell syndication credit for 6 months, which makes their effective price materially cheaper for our early pilot customers.

We would like Redwood to match a similar economic to make the AWS listing compelling for our customers in Q3. Specifically we are asking for either: 1) a 30–35% one-time listing discount for the first year of the listing, or 2) a 20% listing discount plus a one-time syndication credit ($10k–$15k) applied at launch.

Attached is a short pricing comps workbook (CloudBroker_PRICING_COMPS.xlsx) that shows the gap and the revenue profile. We know this is an exception request, so happy to share additional contract terms if it helps. Can you advise who we should work with at Redwood to get a quick decision? We are aiming to publish the AWS listing by 6/18.

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Partnerships
CloudBroker Inc.
(415) 555-0123

---
Attachment: CloudBroker_PRICING_COMPS.xlsx (excel spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice@cloudbroker.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Listing discount request for CloudBroker - AWS marketplace syndication

Ben / Laura — forwarding CloudBroker's ask. Key points: they want to be competitive against EdgeServe and need a compelling AWS listing economics by 6/18. Options they proposed: 30–35% listing discount OR 20% + $10–15k syndication credit.

My read: we should avoid a full 35% list concession if possible. Proposal to expedite: approve 20% listing discount + one-time syndication credit equal to the expected 3 months of co-sell incentive (approx $12k) in exchange for a 12-month commit on consumption/annual contract. This preserves list price integrity while giving them punchy go-to-market dollars.

Attaching my pricing workbook and a private-offer template for paperwork: pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx, private_offer_template.pdf. Ben, can you confirm commercial flexibility? Laura, can you confirm marketplace ops constraints (listing floor, margin minima, co-sell approval) and whether AWS co-sell reps need to be looped in?

If we can agree internally, I'll escalate to Deal Desk/Marcus for formal exception sign-off — we need the exception approved by EOD Friday 6/12 to meet CloudBroker's publishing window.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Account Executive, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx (excel, 200KB); private_offer_template.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

+1 on Priya's recommendation.

I think 20% + a one-time syndication credit (we should target $12k) is an acceptable concession if we secure a 12-month minimum ARR/commit or usage commitment that equals the first-year target. That gives us a predictable revenue floor and helps justify the credit. I approve moving forward with that structure from the commercial side.

Action items:
- Priya: please get a written commitment clause (12-month minimum) in the draft private offer.
- Laura: confirm we can issue a private-offer listing that preserves marketplace rules and record the credit as a separate line item (not a permanent price change).

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Listing discount request for CloudBroker - AWS marketplace syndication

Thanks for the summary. A few operational constraints to flag before we escalate:

1) Marketplace policy: we can't publish a listing with a net price that violates our internal minimum margin floor. The current cost forecast on the workbook looks tight; I attached the relevant policy excerpt (marketplace_policy_excerpt.pdf).
2) Private offer vs listing price: I agree on using a private offer (not permanent list change). Private offers can include one-off credits — that aligns well.
3) AWS co-sell: we should loop in Mark Jones (AWS Partner) to ensure the co-sell syndication credit structure doesn't conflict with their incentives. He may ask for a revised co-sell template and forecast.
4) Controls: Deal desk exception required for >15% listing concession or any credit >$8k. So Marcus will need a completed exception form and finance sign-off.

Alternative suggestion: consider a marketplace promo approach — issue a 3-month usage credit applied at launch instead of a headline listing discount. That often preserves list integrity and is easier from a policy perspective. If CloudBroker wants the discount headline, ensure we capture the marketing lift commitment and reporting.

I'll loop Mark on this thread.

Laura Bennett
Marketplace Programs Lead
Redwood Inference

---

Why: This gets CloudBroker published on AWS marketplace by 6/18 and addresses a direct competitive pricing gap vs EdgeServe. We expect the listing + co-sell motion to drive higher ARR expansion across their installed base and increase Redwood visibility in a strategic partner segment.

Required paperwork:
- Completed exception form (I can populate)
- Private-offer draft with 12-month clause
- Finance acknowledgment of credit ($12k) and tracking to marketing/partner spend

Timeline: CloudBroker needs final approval by EOD Friday 6/12 to meet their AWS publishing window.

Please let me know if you'd like a 15-min sync this morning.

Thanks,
Priya
